node.C-1.text:
Old Fei sits on the counterweight of the dead harbour crane, turning a tally board over in his hands. For thirty years he chalked every crew he lifted cargo with into one ledger, and kept that ledger in the tally house by the breakwater.
"Last night I couldn't remember the name of the lad who lost two fingers to the chain," he says. "I knew it yesterday. The Fading's in the tally house. Help me fetch the ledger before it eats the rest."
node.C-2f.text: The door gives at last with a crack that carries across the whole harbour. Inside, the wet page-turning stops. Out on the breakwater a lamp goes grey, and then the one beside it.
node.C-3.text: A swarm of ink has settled on the open ledger like flies on spilt sugar, drinking names line by line. It rises when you step inside, an ink imp drops from the rafters, and two salvage-scavengers who were waiting for it to finish come up out of the dark behind you.
node.C-4.text:
Half the ledger is grey. Old Fei reads what is left with his finger on each line. At the door, a Scriptorium clerk with two hired swords is already waiting.
"That is a register of the living," the clerk says. "The Scriptorium will re-ink it properly. You will be paid." Behind him, an Uninked runner shouts from the breakwater: let the tide have it, names are chains. And Old Fei just holds the book.
node.C-6k.text:
That night Old Fei sits on the crane's counterweight and reads every name still left in the ledger, slowly, out loud, one crew at a time. Some lines come back a little darker as he reads them. When he gets to the lad with two fingers missing he stops, and laughs, and says the name twice.
He presses his old crane token into your hand. "For the next crew."
node.C-6s.text: The clerk sends the copy back three days later: clean gold ink, every surviving line, the grey ones left blank. Old Fei turns the pages for a long time. "It's neat," he says. "They spelled Big Hu wrong."
node.C-6u.text: The ledger turns once in the swell and goes under. The runner salutes you from the breakwater and is gone. Old Fei watches the water for a while. "Maybe they'd rather be free of my chalk," he says, not believing it.
lore.revoked_registry_crane: Thirty years of harbour crews chalked into one book by the crane operator called Old Fei: who lifted, who lost a finger, who was owed a drink. When the Fading reached the tally house it ate the ledger from the back, newest crews first, as if it knew the old man would notice the young ones last.
